Two workloads with the same RPM can consume very different amounts of capacity, so plan and rate-limit by tokens and concurrency instead of RPM alone.\\n* When a request is admitted, the input-token check includes the input tokens plus the requested `max_tokens` value. Set `max_tokens` no higher than your application needs.\\n* Models without published TPM quotas do not currently have per-account TPM quotas exposed in Service Quotas. For Global CRIS, quotas are measured in two dimensions, each serving a distinct purpose in capacity management:\\n\\n* **Tokens per minute (TPM)** \u2013 The maximum number of tokens (input + output) that can be processed per minute.\\n* **Requests per minute (RPM)** \u2013 The maximum number of inference requests that can be made per minute.\\n\\nDefault quotas vary by model and are allocated per source Region. You can view your current quotas in the AWS Service Quotas console by navigating to Amazon Bedrock service quotas in your source Region (Singapore or Jakarta).\\n\\nAmazon Bedrock uses a token burndown rate that weighs output tokens more heavily than input tokens when calculating quota consumption. The burndown rate is 5:1, meaning output tokens consume five times more quota than input tokens because generating tokens requires more computation than processing input.\\n\\n`Quota consumption = Input tokens + (Output tokens \u00d7 5)`\\n\\nFor example, if your request uses 10,000 input tokens and generates 5,000 output tokens:\\n\\n`Total quota consumption = 10,000 + (5,000 \u00d7 5) = 35,000 tokens`\\n\\nThe request consumes 35,000 tokens against your TPM quota for throttling purposes. When planning capacity requirements and requesting quota increases, you need to account for this burndown rate in your calculations. If your application processes requests with this same token pattern at 100 requests per minute, the total quota consumption would be 3,500,000 TPM (100 requests \u00d7 35,000 tokens per request). When working with your AWS Account Manager on quota increase requests, provide your expected request volume, average input tokens per request, and average output tokens per request so they can calculate the appropriate quota allocation using this burndown multiplier\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/global-cross-region-inference-for-latest-anthropic-claude-opus-sonnet-and-haiku-models-on-amazon-bedrock-in-thailand-malaysia-singapore-indonesia-and-taiwan/\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Access OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock from Canada with cross-Region inference | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"## Quota management\\n\\nCross-Region inference quotas on the `bedrock-runtime` endpoint are measured in tokens per minute (TPM) per model. Each quota combines input and output tokens against a single limit. US geographic and global inference profiles have separate quota allocations, so switching between them changes the pool you draw from.\\n\\nToken consumption combines input tokens, cache-write input tokens, and output tokens. Output tokens are multiplied by the model\u2019s burndown rate, so output-heavy workloads consume quota faster than raw token counts suggest. Before a production rollout, request quota increases early and monitor quota utilization. Test with representative prompts, output lengths, streaming behavior, concurrency, and peak traffic.\\n\\nTo request a quota increase, follow these steps:\\n\\n1. Open the Service Quotas console in `ca-central-1` or `ca-west-1`.\\n2. Choose **Amazon Bedrock**, then select the quota named \u201cCross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute\u201d for the model that you need.\\n3. Choose **Request increase at account level**, enter your target value, and submit the request.\\n\\nFor details on how token usage and costs are tracked, see Track usage and costs in Amazon Bedrock\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/access-openai-gpt-models-on-amazon-bedrock-from-canada-with-cross-region-inference/\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot the \\\"ThrottlingException\\\" error when I use Amazon Bedrock on-demand resources?\",\"context\":\"### Monitor your AWS service quotas\\n\\nReview your [Amazon Bedrock service quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas.html) to make sure that you didn't exceed them. Check Amazon CloudWatch metrics at 1-minute increments to identify throttling patterns. When your usage exceeds the quotas at peak times, resource throttle can occur even with previously successful batches. To make sure that your application's request volume doesn't exceed the quotas, monitor the\u00a0**InputTokenCount** and **Invocations** [Amazon Bedrock runtime metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/monitoring-runtime-metrics.html).\\n\\nSpecific models have separate quotas for Requests Per Minute (RPM) and Tokens Per Minute (TPM) that Amazon Bedrock enforces concurrently.\\n\\nNewer model versions can have different quotas than previous versions.\\n\\n**Note:** The Service Quota dashboard shows only configured quotas, not real-time usage. To monitor real-time usage, use CloudWatch\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-throttling-error\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Search Bedrock docs on mantle endpoint quotas and usage types"}

Amazon Bedrock provides two inference endpoints. The endpoint you choose determines which APIs and features are available.\\\\n\\\\nFor most new applications, use the `bedrock-runtime` endpoint. Use `bedrock-mantle` when you specifically need capabilities that are currently available only there, such as server-side and pre-configured tools (including web search), background inference, Projects, or Workspaces. To see which endpoint each model supports, see Endpoint availability. The following table compares the two endpoints.\\\\n\\\\n| **Endpoint** | **Supported APIs** | **Description** |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| `bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com` (recommended) | InvokeModel / Converse / Chat Completions / Responses API / Messages API | Region-specific endpoints for making inference requests for models hosted in Amazon Bedrock using the InvokeModel/Converse/Chat Completions/Responses/Messages APIs. For more information about the Bedrock-native operations, see Amazon Bedrock Runtime API operations. The OpenAI-compatible APIs are called on the `/openai/v1` paths of this endpoint rather than through the AWS SDKs. |\\\\n| `bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws` | Responses API / Chat Completions API / Messages API | Region-specific endpoints for making inference requests for models hosted in Amazon Bedrock using the OpenAI-compatible endpoints and the Anthropic Messages API. |\\\\n\\\\n**Note:**\\\\n\\\\nBoth endpoints use the same underlying Mantle inference engine. The `bedrock-mantle` name identifies an endpoint surface, not a different inference engine.\\\\n\\\\nExisting applications that use `bedrock-mantle` continue to be fully supported and do not need to change. Both endpoints let you bring an existing OpenAI SDK codebase to Amazon Bedrock by changing only the base URL and API key, and both support the OpenAI-compatible Responses and Chat Completions APIs and the Anthropic Messages API.\\\\n\\\\nAPI support\\\\n\\\\n| API | `bedrock-runtime` | `bedrock-mantle` |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| InvokeModel | | |\\\\n| Converse / ConverseStream | | |\\\\n| Chat Completions (OpenAI-compatible) | | |\\\\n| Responses API (OpenAI-compatible) | | |\\\\n| Messages API (Anthropic-native) |\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Run open weight models on Amazon Bedrock in AWS European Sovereign Cloud | AWS Security Blog\",\"context\":\"## Next generation inference engine for Amazon Bedrock\\\\n\\\\nThe inference engine is a distributed engine for serving large-scale machine learning models, built for high performance, reliability, and security. You reach it through the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, which supports OpenAI-compatible APIs (the Responses and Chat Completions APIs). You can bring an existing OpenAI SDK codebase to Amazon Bedrock by changing only the base URL and API key. The Responses API supports stateful conversation management, which rebuilds context without you passing conversation history with each request. Stored responses are scoped by Amazon Bedrock project, a logical boundary that represents a workload for access control, cost tracking, and usage monitoring.\\\\n\\\\nThe engine applies the same operational security practices you rely on across AWS. Access follows a least privilege model, where each operator has access only to the systems a specific task requires, and only for the time that privilege is needed. Any access to systems that store or process customer data or metadata is logged, monitored for anomalies, and audited. All your prompts and responses are kept private during inference\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/run-open-weight-models-on-aws-bedrock-in-aws-european-sovereign-cloud/\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Responses API\",\"context\":\"# Responses API\\\\n\\\\nAmazon Bedrock provides the OpenAI Responses API on both the `bedrock-runtime` and\\\\n`bedrock-mantle` endpoints. Use `bedrock-runtime` for new\\\\napplications. Use `bedrock-mantle` only when a model or capability that you\\\\nrequire isn\\'t available on `bedrock-runtime`.\\\\n\\\\n| **Endpoint** | **Base URL** | **When to use** |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| `bedrock-runtime` (recommended) | `https://bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com/openai/v1` | New applications and migrations when the required model and Responses API features are supported. |\\\\n| `bedrock-mantle` (compatibility) | `https://bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws/v1` | Existing applications and workloads that require Mantle-only support, such as Responses API access to GPT OSS models, background inference, or server-side tools. |\\\\n\\\\n**Note:**\\\\n\\\\nOn `bedrock-mantle`, the path prefix varies by model. Most models are served\\\\nunder `/v1`, as shown in the preceding table, but some are served under\\\\n`/openai/v1` instead. A request that uses the wrong prefix for a model is\\\\nrejected with `model `<model-id>` isn\\'t supported on this\\\\nroute`. To confirm the base URL for a specific model, see the\\\\n**Programmatic Access** table on its card in\\\\nModels at a glance.\\\\n\\\\nThe two endpoints don\\'t have identical feature support. Requests on\\\\n`bedrock-runtime` are always synchronous, server-side tools aren\\'t available, and\\\\nonly the default project is supported. For the full comparison, see Inference endpoints supported by Amazon Bedrock,\\\\nand for the details of each difference, see Using the Responses API on the bedrock-runtime endpoint.\\\\n\\\\n**Important:**\\\\n\\\\nWhen using the OpenAI SDK with Amazon Bedrock, you must point it to the Amazon Bedrock endpoint, not the OpenAI endpoint. Set the following environment variables, choosing the base URL for the endpoint you want:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\n# bedrock-runtime (recommended)\\\\nOPENAI_BASE_URL=\\\\\"https://bedrock-runtime.<your-region>.amazonaws.com/openai/v1\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n# bedrock-mantle\\\\nOPENAI_BASE_URL=\\\\\"https://bedrock-mantle.<your-region>.api.aws/v1\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nOPENAI_API_KEY=\\\\\"<your Bedrock API key>\\\\\"\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-responses-api.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Introducing cross-Region inference for OpenAI GPT-5.6 models on Amazon Bedrock | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"### Choosing between Amazon Bedrock Mantle and Runtime endpoints\\\\n\\\\nFor new applications, we recommend the bedrock-runtime endpoint. Shared across all APIs served by the endpoint for that model. |\\n| Bedrock Mantle output tokens per minute for `${model}` | Per model, per Region | The maximum number of output tokens per minute that the model can generate for your account on the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint. Throttling is governed solely by the input and output token quotas described in this section.\\n\\n## How requests are evaluated against quotas\\n\\nWhen you submit an inference request to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, AWS evaluates it against your quotas in the following order:\\n\\n1. **Input tokens per minute** \u2013 The number of input tokens in the request, plus the value of `max_tokens` (or the model-specific maximum if `max_tokens` is not set), is checked against the input-tokens-per-minute quota for the requested model. To request an increase, submit a request through the AWS Support limit increase form and select **Amazon Bedrock** as the service. In your request, specify:\\n\\n* The endpoint (`bedrock-mantle`).\\n* The Region.\\n* The model.\\n* The quota name (input TPM or output TPM) and the value you are requesting.\\n\\nYou can request increases to input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute for the same model in a single support case. Unlike traditional compute resources where costs scale predictably with instance hours, with Amazon Bedrock one misconfigured application can use millions of tokens in minutes. Retry loops that don't back off, prompts that pass entire documents without truncation, and batch jobs without concurrency controls sometimes generate significant unexpected charges.\\n\\nThe challenge is timing. - **`bedrock-mantle`:** it has separate "Bedrock Mantle input tokens per minute" and "output tokens per minute" quotas for each model and Region. It has no RPM quota.
  - The input check counts your input tokens plus `max_tokens`. Cached input reads don't count.
- **`bedrock-runtime`:** it has a single combined TPM quota for each model. Output tokens are weighted by a burndown rate, and the limit covers input and output together.

**How to find out which quota applies to you**
1. Check your application or SDK configuration for the base URL. `bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws` means the Mantle quotas apply. `bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com` means the runtime quotas apply. This is the most reliable check.
2. Look at the API you call. `InvokeModel` and `Converse` exist only on `bedrock-runtime`. Server-side tools, background inference and Projects exist only on `bedrock-mantle`.
3. If you're being throttled, look at the 429 responses and the Service Quotas console. Search for "Bedrock Mantle" to see whether a Mantle quota exists for the model and how close you are to it.
4. Also check whether you route through a gateway or proxy, since that can hide the real endpoint from your own code.
